# Requirement
```text
 Overall/Domain description.
 Console pipe-connection game: grid with outer walls, one source inside pointing inward, one sink on the border
  pointing outward. Player places pipes from a queue; after a delay, water flows along placed pipes.
Cell[][] uses 0-based array indices, but index 0 and rows-1/cols-1 are occupied by the outer wall border. Therefore, the playable area starts at internal index 1: [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2]. Player-facing coordinates are deliberately aligned with these playable indices: row 1 maps to internal row 1, column 'A' maps to internal col 1. No row-1/col-1 conversion is performed.
 Direction provides four directions plus opposite/offset; PipeShape defines
  connection
  directions; TerminationType distinguishes SOURCE vs SINK.

  Functional Requirements

Coordinate and Direction: Coordinate.row and Coordinate.col represent internal Cell[][] array indices and are used directly as cells[row][col]. A Cell stored at cells[r][c] should have Coordinate(row=r, col=c). 
Because the outer wall border occupies index 0, playable cells naturally start at index 1, so player input aligns with internal playable indices.
  Direction enum provides four directions (UP, DOWN, LEFT, RIGHT) and Pa19Helper provides getOpposite() returning the opposite direction
  and getOffset() returning the unit coordinate offset for movement calculations.

  Game: Operations to place a pipe, skip, undo, advance water flow, check win, check loss; convenience fromString
  constructor; maintain step count. 
Operation placePipe: This method maps the player column letter to an internal column index using col - 'A' + 1, 
keeps row unchanged, and places the pipe at cells[row][colIndex]. For example, placePipe(1, 'A') targets cells[1][1].
Operation skipPipe: Consumes the current pipe from the queue and increments the step count. Operation
  undoStep: Pops the last placed cell from CellStack, restores the pipe to the queue head, clears the cell on the map,
  and increments the step count. Returns false if there are no steps to undo.

  Map: Cells are stored as a 2D array Cell[][] with indices [0..rows-1] × [0..cols-1],
  where index 0 and rows-1/cols-1 are walls (border). The playable area occupies
  internal indices [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2], which aligns with 1-based
  user input mapping. tryPlacePipe(row, col, pipe) accepts playable-area aligned coordinates (row and col in [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2]) and uses them
  directly as array indices (no conversion needed due to the wall alignment).
  It rejects: (1) row/col outside [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2], (2) non-FillableCell,
  or (3) already-occupied cell.

  Cell family: Cell.fromChar parses map chars to concrete cells; FillableCell holds an optional pipe and renders pipe or
  '.'; TerminationCell holds pointingTo direction and Type (SOURCE/SINK), with filled state for rendering; Wall renders
  wall char.

  TerminationCell.toSingleChar: Returns the corresponding arrow character based on the current termination cell's
  filling state and pointingTo direction: when filled, returns the arrow from PipePatterns.Filled; when unfilled,
  returns the arrow from PipePatterns.Unfilled. Both SOURCE and SINK use pointingTo directly without direction reversal.
  Throws IllegalStateException("Invalid pointingTo value!") for unknown direction.

  Pipe: Expose connection directions via getConnections() returning Direction[] based on Shape; char rendering by
  filled/unfilled state; construct from short string code (HZ, VT, TL, TR, BL, BR, CR). getConnections(): Returns the
  list of connection directions based on the current pipe shape; throws IllegalStateException("Unknown shape") if the
  shape is not recognized. toSingleChar(): Returns the character representation of this pipe, different for filled and
  unfilled pipes.

  Water Flow: fillBeginTile() marks the source cell as filled. fillTiles(distance) fills pipes within the specified
  distance from source using BFS-style expansion. Water propagates along pipes only when adjacent pipes have matching
  connection directions (one pipe's direction must be the opposite of the other). Each round increments the fill
  distance by 1.

  Win/Loss Conditions: checkPath() uses BFS to determine if a connected path exists from SOURCE to SINK by following
  (i) from SOURCE, step once in the SOURCE pointingTo direction, and (ii) from a pipe cell, step in each pipe connection direction.
  It does not require the traversed pipes to be filled; reaching the SINK cell implies win. hasLost() returns true when prevFilledTiles == 0,
  meaning no new pipes were filled in the previous round (loss condition). The game checks loss only after delay has ended (distance > 0).

  PipeQueue: peek/consume/undo head pipe and auto-refill to fixed length with random shapes. undo(Pipe) inserts the pipe
  back to the front of the queue.

  DelayBar: countdown() decrements the current value by 1 each round. distance() returns -currentValue, representing how
  far the water should flow (negative during countdown, positive after delay ends).

  CellStack: push/pop last placement; undoCount counts the number of successful undo actions (i.e., successful pop
  operations), not the current stack size; 

  External/Tool Classes (not generated; handwritten or reused,You only need to assume that these Java files mentioned below are already in the pa19 package.)
  Pa19Helper is a small helper/assembly class used to build core game model objects for this project. It provides
  convenience methods to (1) construct a Game by wiring together Map, PipeQueue, DelayBar, and CellStack from given
  inputs, and (2) create/parse basic elements (e.g., Map from a Cell[][] or string representation, map characters/short

  Deserializer: Purpose: deserialize map input into runtime objects. Field: Path path (input file path). Constructors:

# Operation Specifications
Map::undo
Summary: Clears the pipe at the given coordinate on the map, used as part of Game::undoStep to remove a previously placed pipe.
Algorithm:
  1. Look up cells[coord.row][coord.col].
  2. If it is a FillableCell, set its `pipe` reference to null.
  3. If the coordinate lies in `filledTiles`, remove it (so future fill computations are consistent).
Related Features: `cell` grid; `filledTiles` list.
Related Classes: FillableCell, Coordinate
Input: Coordinate coord - the coordinate of the cell whose pipe should be cleared.
Output: void
Pre-condition: `coord` corresponds to a cell that was previously placed (typically from a popped FillableCell).
Post-condition: The cell's pipe is null and (if applicable) the coordinate has been removed from the filled-tiles set.

Map::tryPlacePipe
Summary: Attempts to place the given pipe on the cell at the supplied playable-area-aligned (row, col) coordinates. Rejects placements that are out of bounds, target a non-FillableCell, or target an already-occupied cell.
Algorithm:
  1. Validate that row and col are within the playable area [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2]; if not, return false.
  2. Look up cells[row][col]; if it is not a FillableCell, return false.
  3. If the FillableCell already has a non-null pipe, return false (already occupied).
  4. Otherwise, set the FillableCell's pipe to the supplied pipe and return true.
Related Features: `cell` (Cell[][]) the 2D grid; `rows`, `cols` define bounds.
Related Classes: Cell, FillableCell, Pipe, Coordinate
Input:
  - int row: playable-area-aligned row index in [1..rows-2].
  - int col: playable-area-aligned column index in [1..cols-2].
  - Pipe pipe: the pipe instance to place.
Output: boolean - true if placement succeeded; false otherwise.
Pre-condition: The map is initialized with a valid grid. Coordinates are already in the internal array index space (no conversion needed).
Post-condition: On true, the pipe is held by the cell at (row, col); on false, no state changes.

Map::fillTiles
Summary: Propagates water through connected pipes using a BFS-style expansion up to the given distance from the source. Each round increments the fill distance by 1. Water moves from a filled cell to an adjacent cell only if the two pipes share matching connection directions (one's direction must be the opposite of the other's).
Algorithm:
  1. Save previous stats: prevFilledDistance, prevFilledTiles = current filled-tile stats (so loss can be detected next round).
  2. Initialize a BFS frontier from all currently filled tiles (after fillBeginTile has been called this round).
  3. For each step in [0..distance-1]:
     a. For each currently filled pipe cell, examine its pipe's connection directions.
     b. For each connection direction d in the pipe:
        i.  Compute the neighbor coordinate via the unit offset of d (e.g., using Pa19Helper.getOffset(d)).
        ii. Verify the neighbor pipe (if any) has a connection whose opposite direction matches d.
        iii. If the neighbor is unfilled and matches, add it to the next frontier and mark it filled.
  4. Update `filledTiles` with all newly filled cells and propagate until the requested distance is reached.
  5. Record the new `prevFilledTiles` and `prevFilledDistance` for the next loss check.
Related Features: `cell` array, `filledTiles` (List<Coordinate>), `prevFilledTiles` (int), `prevFilledDistance` (int), `sourceCell` (TerminationCell) as BFS origin.
Related Classes: Pipe, Coordinate, FillableCell, TerminationCell, Pa19Helper, Direction
Input:
  - int distance: the maximum BFS depth at which to fill pipes this round. Negative during delay (no propagation). 0 means the source is already filled. Positive values advance water outward by that many steps per round.
Output: void
Pre-condition: The map has been initialized with a valid grid, a SOURCE, a SINK, and placed pipes (where applicable). `fillBeginTile` may have been called earlier in the round to mark the source.
Post-condition: `filledTiles` reflects all cells filled by this round's expansion; `prevFilledTiles`/`prevFilledDistance` are updated to current values for subsequent loss detection.

Map::hasLost
Summary: Indicates whether the player has lost, which happens when the previous round produced no new filled tiles (`prevFilledTiles == 0`). This is checked only after the delay has ended (distance > 0).
Algorithm:
  1. Return prevFilledTiles == 0.
Related Features: `prevFilledTiles` (int) records the number of newly filled tiles in the last water-propagation round.
Related Classes: None
Input: None
Output: boolean - true if no new tiles were filled in the most recent propagation round (loss); false otherwise.
Pre-condition: At least one water-propagation round has completed since the delay ended so that `prevFilledTiles` has been updated.
Post-condition: No state is changed.

# Requirement
```text
 Overall/Domain description.
 Console pipe-connection game: grid with outer walls, one source inside pointing inward, one sink on the border
  pointing outward. Player places pipes from a queue; after a delay, water flows along placed pipes.
Cell[][] uses 0-based array indices, but index 0 and rows-1/cols-1 are occupied by the outer wall border. Therefore, the playable area starts at internal index 1: [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2]. Player-facing coordinates are deliberately aligned with these playable indices: row 1 maps to internal row 1, column 'A' maps to internal col 1. No row-1/col-1 conversion is performed.
 Direction provides four directions plus opposite/offset; PipeShape defines
  connection
  directions; TerminationType distinguishes SOURCE vs SINK.

  Functional Requirements

Coordinate and Direction: Coordinate.row and Coordinate.col represent internal Cell[][] array indices and are used directly as cells[row][col]. A Cell stored at cells[r][c] should have Coordinate(row=r, col=c). 
Because the outer wall border occupies index 0, playable cells naturally start at index 1, so player input aligns with internal playable indices.
  Direction enum provides four directions (UP, DOWN, LEFT, RIGHT) and Pa19Helper provides getOpposite() returning the opposite direction
  and getOffset() returning the unit coordinate offset for movement calculations.

  Game: Operations to place a pipe, skip, undo, advance water flow, check win, check loss; convenience fromString
  constructor; maintain step count. 
Operation placePipe: This method maps the player column letter to an internal column index using col - 'A' + 1, 
keeps row unchanged, and places the pipe at cells[row][colIndex]. For example, placePipe(1, 'A') targets cells[1][1].
Operation skipPipe: Consumes the current pipe from the queue and increments the step count. Operation
  undoStep: Pops the last placed cell from CellStack, restores the pipe to the queue head, clears the cell on the map,
  and increments the step count. Returns false if there are no steps to undo.

  Map: Cells are stored as a 2D array Cell[][] with indices [0..rows-1] × [0..cols-1],
  where index 0 and rows-1/cols-1 are walls (border). The playable area occupies
  internal indices [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2], which aligns with 1-based
  user input mapping. tryPlacePipe(row, col, pipe) accepts playable-area aligned coordinates (row and col in [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2]) and uses them
  directly as array indices (no conversion needed due to the wall alignment).
  It rejects: (1) row/col outside [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2], (2) non-FillableCell,
  or (3) already-occupied cell.

  Cell family: Cell.fromChar parses map chars to concrete cells; FillableCell holds an optional pipe and renders pipe or
  '.'; TerminationCell holds pointingTo direction and Type (SOURCE/SINK), with filled state for rendering; Wall renders
  wall char.

  TerminationCell.toSingleChar: Returns the corresponding arrow character based on the current termination cell's
  filling state and pointingTo direction: when filled, returns the arrow from PipePatterns.Filled; when unfilled,
  returns the arrow from PipePatterns.Unfilled. Both SOURCE and SINK use pointingTo directly without direction reversal.
  Throws IllegalStateException("Invalid pointingTo value!") for unknown direction.

  Pipe: Expose connection directions via getConnections() returning Direction[] based on Shape; char rendering by
  filled/unfilled state; construct from short string code (HZ, VT, TL, TR, BL, BR, CR). getConnections(): Returns the
  list of connection directions based on the current pipe shape; throws IllegalStateException("Unknown shape") if the
  shape is not recognized. toSingleChar(): Returns the character representation of this pipe, different for filled and
  unfilled pipes.

  Water Flow: fillBeginTile() marks the source cell as filled. fillTiles(distance) fills pipes within the specified
  distance from source using BFS-style expansion. Water propagates along pipes only when adjacent pipes have matching
  connection directions (one pipe's direction must be the opposite of the other). Each round increments the fill
  distance by 1.

  Win/Loss Conditions: checkPath() uses BFS to determine if a connected path exists from SOURCE to SINK by following
  (i) from SOURCE, step once in the SOURCE pointingTo direction, and (ii) from a pipe cell, step in each pipe connection direction.
  It does not require the traversed pipes to be filled; reaching the SINK cell implies win. hasLost() returns true when prevFilledTiles == 0,
  meaning no new pipes were filled in the previous round (loss condition). The game checks loss only after delay has ended (distance > 0).

  PipeQueue: peek/consume/undo head pipe and auto-refill to fixed length with random shapes. undo(Pipe) inserts the pipe
  back to the front of the queue.

  DelayBar: countdown() decrements the current value by 1 each round. distance() returns -currentValue, representing how
  far the water should flow (negative during countdown, positive after delay ends).

  CellStack: push/pop last placement; undoCount counts the number of successful undo actions (i.e., successful pop
  operations), not the current stack size; 

  External/Tool Classes (not generated; handwritten or reused,You only need to assume that these Java files mentioned below are already in the pa19 package.)
  Pa19Helper is a small helper/assembly class used to build core game model objects for this project. It provides
  convenience methods to (1) construct a Game by wiring together Map, PipeQueue, DelayBar, and CellStack from given
  inputs, and (2) create/parse basic elements (e.g., Map from a Cell[][] or string representation, map characters/short
  codes into Cell/Pipe). It also centralizes simple direction utilities (opposite direction and unit offsets) used
  during parsing and movement-related calculations.
  Deserializer: Purpose: deserialize map input into runtime objects. Field: Path path (input file path). Constructors:
  Deserializer(String path) delegates to private Deserializer(Path); private Deserializer(Path) validates file existence
  and throws FileNotFoundException if missing. Methods: Game parseGame() reads rows, cols, delay, map lines, and
  optional default pipes, then returns Pa19Helper.createGame(...); on unexpected EOF or I/O failure, returns null
  (and logs error). static Cell[][] parseString(int rows, int cols, String cellsRep) converts multiline text to a Cell
  matrix by character, using Pa19Helper.cellFromChar with SINK type on border cells and SOURCE type on inner
  cells. private String getFirstNonEmptyLine(BufferedReader br) returns the first non-blank, non-comment line (ignores
  lines starting with #), or null at end of stream.

  PipePatterns: Purpose: central constant repository for all map-rendering characters. Design: final utility class with
  private constructor (non-instantiable). Exposed constants: WALL (solid wall block), plus two nested static groups:
  Filled and Unfilled. Each group defines arrow chars (UP_ARROW, DOWN_ARROW, LEFT_ARROW, RIGHT_ARROW) and pipe-shape
  chars (HORIZONTAL, VERTICAL, TOP_LEFT, TOP_RIGHT, BOTTOM_LEFT, BOTTOM_RIGHT, CROSS). Use PipePatterns constants for
  all rendering chars; do not hardcode glyphs in TerminationCell and PipeShape logic.

  StringUtils: Purpose: provide lightweight string helper utilities. Class design: utility class with a private
  constructor to prevent instantiation. 
```

# Operation Specifications
Map::undo
Summary: Clears the pipe at the given coordinate on the map, used as part of Game::undoStep to remove a previously placed pipe.
Algorithm:
  1. Look up cells[coord.row][coord.col].
  2. If it is a FillableCell, set its `pipe` reference to null.
  3. If the coordinate lies in `filledTiles`, remove it (so future fill computations are consistent).
Related Features: `cell` grid; `filledTiles` list.
Related Classes: FillableCell, Coordinate
Input: Coordinate coord - the coordinate of the cell whose pipe should be cleared.
Output: void
Pre-condition: `coord` corresponds to a cell that was previously placed (typically from a popped FillableCell).
Post-condition: The cell's pipe is null and (if applicable) the coordinate has been removed from the filled-tiles set.

Map::tryPlacePipe
Summary: Attempts to place the given pipe on the cell at the supplied playable-area-aligned (row, col) coordinates. Rejects placements that are out of bounds, target a non-FillableCell, or target an already-occupied cell.
Algorithm:
  1. Validate that row and col are within the playable area [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2]; if not, return false.
  2. Look up cells[row][col]; if it is not a FillableCell, return false.
  3. If the FillableCell already has a non-null pipe, return false (already occupied).
  4. Otherwise, set the FillableCell's pipe to the supplied pipe and return true.
Related Features: `cell` (Cell[][]) the 2D grid; `rows`, `cols` define bounds.
Related Classes: Cell, FillableCell, Pipe, Coordinate
Input:
  - int row: playable-area-aligned row index in [1..rows-2].
  - int col: playable-area-aligned column index in [1..cols-2].
  - Pipe pipe: the pipe instance to place.
Output: boolean - true if placement succeeded; false otherwise.
Pre-condition: The map is initialized with a valid grid. Coordinates are already in the internal array index space (no conversion needed).
Post-condition: On true, the pipe is held by the cell at (row, col); on false, no state changes.

Map::fillTiles
Summary: Propagates water through connected pipes using a BFS-style expansion up to the given distance from the source. Each round increments the fill distance by 1. Water moves from a filled cell to an adjacent cell only if the two pipes share matching connection directions (one's direction must be the opposite of the other's).
Algorithm:
  1. Save previous stats: prevFilledDistance, prevFilledTiles = current filled-tile stats (so loss can be detected next round).
  2. Initialize a BFS frontier from all currently filled tiles (after fillBeginTile has been called this round).
  3. For each step in [0..distance-1]:
     a. For each currently filled pipe cell, examine its pipe's connection directions.
     b. For each connection direction d in the pipe:
        i.  Compute the neighbor coordinate via the unit offset of d (e.g., using Pa19Helper.getOffset(d)).
        ii. Verify the neighbor pipe (if any) has a connection whose opposite direction matches d.
        iii. If the neighbor is unfilled and matches, add it to the next frontier and mark it filled.
  4. Update `filledTiles` with all newly filled cells and propagate until the requested distance is reached.
  5. Record the new `prevFilledTiles` and `prevFilledDistance` for the next loss check.
Related Features: `cell` array, `filledTiles` (List<Coordinate>), `prevFilledTiles` (int), `prevFilledDistance` (int), `sourceCell` (TerminationCell) as BFS origin.
Related Classes: Pipe, Coordinate, FillableCell, TerminationCell, Pa19Helper, Direction
Input:
  - int distance: the maximum BFS depth at which to fill pipes this round. Negative during delay (no propagation). 0 means the source is already filled. Positive values advance water outward by that many steps per round.
Output: void
Pre-condition: The map has been initialized with a valid grid, a SOURCE, a SINK, and placed pipes (where applicable). `fillBeginTile` may have been called earlier in the round to mark the source.
Post-condition: `filledTiles` reflects all cells filled by this round's expansion; `prevFilledTiles`/`prevFilledDistance` are updated to current values for subsequent loss detection.

Map::hasLost
Summary: Indicates whether the player has lost, which happens when the previous round produced no new filled tiles (`prevFilledTiles == 0`). This is checked only after the delay has ended (distance > 0).
Algorithm:
  1. Return prevFilledTiles == 0.
Related Features: `prevFilledTiles` (int) records the number of newly filled tiles in the last water-propagation round.
Related Classes: None
Input: None
Output: boolean - true if no new tiles were filled in the most recent propagation round (loss); false otherwise.
Pre-condition: At least one water-propagation round has completed since the delay ended so that `prevFilledTiles` has been updated.
Post-condition: No state is changed.

  External/Tool Classes (not generated; handwritten or reused,You only need to assume that these Java files mentioned below are already in the pa19 package.)
  Pa19Helper is a small helper/assembly class used to build core game model objects for this project. It provides
  convenience methods to (1) construct a Game by wiring together Map, PipeQueue, DelayBar, and CellStack from given
  inputs, and (2) create/parse basic elements (e.g., Map from a Cell[][] or string representation, map characters/short
  codes into Cell/Pipe). It also centralizes simple direction utilities (opposite direction and unit offsets) used
  during parsing and movement-related calculations.
  Deserializer: Purpose: deserialize map input into runtime objects. Field: Path path (input file path). Constructors:
  Deserializer(String path) delegates to private Deserializer(Path); private Deserializer(Path) validates file existence
  and throws FileNotFoundException if missing. Methods: Game parseGame() reads rows, cols, delay, map lines, and
  optional default pipes, then returns Pa19Helper.createGame(...); on unexpected EOF or I/O failure, returns null
  (and logs error). static Cell[][] parseString(int rows, int cols, String cellsRep) converts multiline text to a Cell
  matrix by character, using Pa19Helper.cellFromChar with SINK type on border cells and SOURCE type on inner
  cells. private String getFirstNonEmptyLine(BufferedReader br) returns the first non-blank, non-comment line (ignores
  lines starting with #), or null at end of stream.

  PipePatterns: Purpose: central constant repository for all map-rendering characters. Design: final utility class with
  private constructor (non-instantiable). Exposed constants: WALL (solid wall block), plus two nested static groups:
  Filled and Unfilled. Each group defines arrow chars (UP_ARROW, DOWN_ARROW, LEFT_ARROW, RIGHT_ARROW) and pipe-shape
  chars (HORIZONTAL, VERTICAL, TOP_LEFT, TOP_RIGHT, BOTTOM_LEFT, BOTTOM_RIGHT, CROSS). Use PipePatterns constants for
  all rendering chars; do not hardcode glyphs in TerminationCell and PipeShape logic.

  StringUtils: Purpose: provide lightweight string helper utilities. Class design: utility class with a private
  constructor to prevent instantiation.

# Operation Specifications
Game::undoStep
Summary: Undoes the most recent successful pipe placement: removes the pipe from the map, restores it to the head of the pipe queue, and increments the step counter. Returns false if there is nothing to undo.
Algorithm:
  1. Pop the last placed FillableCell from cellStack via cellStack.pop().
  2. If the popped cell is null (nothing to undo), return false.
  3. Identify the cell's Coordinate (row, col).
  4. Read the pipe currently held by the popped cell.
  5. Restore the pipe to the front of the queue via pipeQueue.undo(pipe).
  6. Clear the cell on the map via map.undo(coord).
  7. Increment numOfSteps by 1.
  8. Return true.
Related Features: `numOfSteps` incremented; coordinates from the popped cell; cell stack's pop increments its undo counter.
Related Classes: CellStack, PipeQueue, Map, FillableCell, Coordinate, Pipe
Input: None
Output: boolean - true if an undo was performed; false if the cell stack was empty (no steps to undo).
Pre-condition: The Game has been initialized. If no successful placements have been made, this operation must return false.
Post-condition: The most recent placed pipe is removed from the map, returned to the queue's head, and `numOfSteps` is incremented by 1. The CellStack's undo count is also incremented.

Game::placePipe
Summary: Places the head pipe from the queue at the cell identified by the given player-facing row and column letter, advancing the game state (consuming the pipe, recording the placement, and incrementing the step counter) if the placement is valid.
Algorithm:
  1. Convert column letter to internal column index: colIndex = col - 'A' + 1.
  2. Keep `row` unchanged (player row 1 corresponds to internal row 1; playable area starts at index 1).
  3. If row or colIndex is outside the playable area [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2], return false (no state change).
  4. Read the head pipe via pipeQueue.peek(); if null, return false.
  5. Attempt to place the pipe via map.tryPlacePipe(row, colIndex, headPipe).
  6. If placement is successful:
     a. Push the cell (with the placed pipe) onto cellStack via cellStack.push(...).
     b. Consume the head pipe via pipeQueue.consume().
     c. Increment numOfSteps by 1.
     d. Return true.
  7. Otherwise, return false.
Related Features: `numOfSteps` (int) tracks total steps taken; delegates to pipe queue and map for placement; cell stack for undo support.
Related Classes: Map, PipeQueue, CellStack, FillableCell, Pipe, Coordinate
Input:
  - int row: 1-based player row index, which equals the internal array row index (range: [1..rows-2]).
  - char col: uppercase column letter starting at 'A' for internal col 1 (range: 'A'..column corresponding to cols-2).
Output: boolean - true if the pipe was successfully placed; false if the location is invalid or occupied.
Pre-condition: The Game has been initialized with a valid map, pipe queue, and cell stack; `col` is an uppercase letter; `row` is in [1..rows-2].
Post-condition: On true, the head pipe is removed from the queue, the cell is now occupied and pushed onto the undo stack, and `numOfSteps` is incremented by 1. On false, no state changes occur.

Game::hasLost
Summary: Reports whether the player has lost the current game, which is true when the water flow made no progress in the previous round (i.e., no new pipes were filled) and the delay has already ended.
Algorithm:
  1. Return map.hasLost().
Related Features: Delegates entirely to the underlying map's loss state.
Related Classes: Map
Input: None
Output: boolean - true if no tiles were filled in the last water propagation round (and the delay has ended); false otherwise.
Pre-condition: The Game has been initialized and a map exists.
Post-condition: No state is changed by this query.

Game::updateState
Summary: Advances the game state for one round: ticks the delay bar, then triggers the map to begin filling from the source and propagate water by the appropriate distance.
Algorithm:
  1. Decrement the delay bar by calling delayBar.countdown().
  2. Read the propagation distance via delayBar.distance().
  3. If distance >= 0 (delay has ended), call map.fillBeginTile() to mark the source as filled.
  4. Call map.fillTiles(distance) to advance water flow by the appropriate distance.
Related Features: Delegates to delayBar and map; the map tracks `prevFilledTiles`/`prevFilledDistance` for loss detection.
Related Classes: DelayBar, Map
Input: None
Output: void
Pre-condition: The Game has been initialized and at least one round of play has begun.
Post-condition: The delay bar has been decremented and the map's filled-tile state has been updated for this round; loss conditions can subsequently be queried via hasLost().

Game::skipPipe
Summary: Skips the current pipe by consuming it from the head of the queue without placing it, and increments the step counter.
Algorithm:
  1. If pipeQueue is empty (no head pipe), do nothing and return.
  2. Consume the head pipe via pipeQueue.consume().
  3. Increment numOfSteps by 1.
Related Features: `numOfSteps` is incremented; delegates to PipeQueue.
Related Classes: PipeQueue
Input: None
Output: void
Pre-condition: The Game has been initialized and the pipe queue has at least one pipe (or the operation is a no-op).
Post-condition: The head pipe is removed from the queue and `numOfSteps` is incremented by 1.

Game::hasWon
Summary: Reports whether the player has won the current game, which is true when a connected path from SOURCE to SINK exists following the rules of `Map.checkPath()`.
Algorithm:
  1. Return map.checkPath().
Related Features: Delegates entirely to the underlying map's win check.
Related Classes: Map
Input: None
Output: boolean - true if the source is connected to the sink; false otherwise.
Pre-condition: The Game has been initialized and a map exists.
Post-condition: No state is changed by this query.

# Requirement
```text
 Overall/Domain description.
 Console pipe-connection game: grid with outer walls, one source inside pointing inward, one sink on the border
  pointing outward. Player places pipes from a queue; after a delay, water flows along placed pipes.
Cell[][] uses 0-based array indices, but index 0 and rows-1/cols-1 are occupied by the outer wall border. Therefore, the playable area starts at internal index 1: [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2]. Player-facing coordinates are deliberately aligned with these playable indices: row 1 maps to internal row 1, column 'A' maps to internal col 1. No row-1/col-1 conversion is performed.
 Direction provides four directions plus opposite/offset; PipeShape defines
  connection
  directions; TerminationType distinguishes SOURCE vs SINK.

  Functional Requirements

Coordinate and Direction: Coordinate.row and Coordinate.col represent internal Cell[][] array indices and are used directly as cells[row][col]. A Cell stored at cells[r][c] should have Coordinate(row=r, col=c). 
Because the outer wall border occupies index 0, playable cells naturally start at index 1, so player input aligns with internal playable indices.
  Direction enum provides four directions (UP, DOWN, LEFT, RIGHT) and Pa19Helper provides getOpposite() returning the opposite direction
  and getOffset() returning the unit coordinate offset for movement calculations.

  Game: Operations to place a pipe, skip, undo, advance water flow, check win, check loss; convenience fromString
  constructor; maintain step count. 
Operation placePipe: This method maps the player column letter to an internal column index using col - 'A' + 1, 
keeps row unchanged, and places the pipe at cells[row][colIndex]. For example, placePipe(1, 'A') targets cells[1][1].
Operation skipPipe: Consumes the current pipe from the queue and increments the step count. Operation
  undoStep: Pops the last placed cell from CellStack, restores the pipe to the queue head, clears the cell on the map,
  and increments the step count. Returns false if there are no steps to undo.

  Map: Cells are stored as a 2D array Cell[][] with indices [0..rows-1] × [0..cols-1],
  where index 0 and rows-1/cols-1 are walls (border). The playable area occupies
  internal indices [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2], which aligns with 1-based
  user input mapping. tryPlacePipe(row, col, pipe) accepts playable-area aligned coordinates (row and col in [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2]) and uses them
  directly as array indices (no conversion needed due to the wall alignment).
  It rejects: (1) row/col outside [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2], (2) non-FillableCell,
  or (3) already-occupied cell.

  Cell family: Cell.fromChar parses map chars to concrete cells; FillableCell holds an optional pipe and renders pipe or
  '.'; TerminationCell holds pointingTo direction and Type (SOURCE/SINK), with filled state for rendering; Wall renders
  wall char.

  TerminationCell.toSingleChar: Returns the corresponding arrow character based on the current termination cell's
  filling state and pointingTo direction: when filled, returns the arrow from PipePatterns.Filled; when unfilled,
  returns the arrow from PipePatterns.Unfilled. Both SOURCE and SINK use pointingTo directly without direction reversal.
  Throws IllegalStateException("Invalid pointingTo value!") for unknown direction.

  Pipe: Expose connection directions via getConnections() returning Direction[] based on Shape; char rendering by
  filled/unfilled state; construct from short string code (HZ, VT, TL, TR, BL, BR, CR). getConnections(): Returns the
  list of connection directions based on the current pipe shape; throws IllegalStateException("Unknown shape") if the
  shape is not recognized. toSingleChar(): Returns the character representation of this pipe, different for filled and
  unfilled pipes.

  Water Flow: fillBeginTile() marks the source cell as filled. fillTiles(distance) fills pipes within the specified
  distance from source using BFS-style expansion. Water propagates along pipes only when adjacent pipes have matching
  connection directions (one pipe's direction must be the opposite of the other). Each round increments the fill
  distance by 1.

  Win/Loss Conditions: checkPath() uses BFS to determine if a connected path exists from SOURCE to SINK by following
  (i) from SOURCE, step once in the SOURCE pointingTo direction, and (ii) from a pipe cell, step in each pipe connection direction.
  It does not require the traversed pipes to be filled; reaching the SINK cell implies win. hasLost() returns true when prevFilledTiles == 0,
  meaning no new pipes were filled in the previous round (loss condition). The game checks loss only after delay has ended (distance > 0).

  PipeQueue: peek/consume/undo head pipe and auto-refill to fixed length with random shapes. undo(Pipe) inserts the pipe
  back to the front of the queue.

  DelayBar: countdown() decrements the current value by 1 each round. distance() returns -currentValue, representing how
  far the water should flow (negative during countdown, positive after delay ends).

  CellStack: push/pop last placement; undoCount counts the number of successful undo actions (i.e., successful pop
  operations), not the current stack size; 

  External/Tool Classes (not generated; handwritten or reused,You only need to assume that these Java files mentioned below are already in the pa19 package.)
  Pa19Helper is a small helper/assembly class used to build core game model objects for this project. It provides
  convenience methods to (1) construct a Game by wiring together Map, PipeQueue, DelayBar, and CellStack from given
  inputs, and (2) create/parse basic elements (e.g., Map from a Cell[][] or string representation, map characters/short
  codes into Cell/Pipe). It also centralizes simple direction utilities (opposite direction and unit offsets) used
  during parsing and movement-related calculations.
  Deserializer: Purpose: deserialize map input into runtime objects. Field: Path path (input file path). Constructors:
  Deserializer(String path) delegates to private Deserializer(Path); private Deserializer(Path) validates file existence
  and throws FileNotFoundException if missing. Methods: Game parseGame() reads rows, cols, delay, map lines, and
  optional default pipes, then returns Pa19Helper.createGame(...); on unexpected EOF or I/O failure, returns null
  (and logs error). static Cell[][] parseString(int rows, int cols, String cellsRep) converts multiline text to a Cell
  matrix by character, using Pa19Helper.cellFromChar with SINK type on border cells and SOURCE type on inner
  cells. private String getFirstNonEmptyLine(BufferedReader br) returns the first non-blank, non-comment line (ignores
  lines starting with #), or null at end of stream.

  PipePatterns: Purpose: central constant repository for all map-rendering characters. Design: final utility class with
  private constructor (non-instantiable). Exposed constants: WALL (solid wall block), plus two nested static groups:
  Filled and Unfilled. Each group defines arrow chars (UP_ARROW, DOWN_ARROW, LEFT_ARROW, RIGHT_ARROW) and pipe-shape
  chars (HORIZONTAL, VERTICAL, TOP_LEFT, TOP_RIGHT, BOTTOM_LEFT, BOTTOM_RIGHT, CROSS). Use PipePatterns constants for
  all rendering chars; do not hardcode glyphs in TerminationCell and PipeShape logic.

  StringUtils: Purpose: provide lightweight string helper utilities. Class design: utility class with a private
  constructor to prevent instantiation.

  4. Call map.fillTiles(distance) to advance water flow by the appropriate distance.
Related Features: Delegates to delayBar and map; the map tracks `prevFilledTiles`/`prevFilledDistance` for loss detection.
Related Classes: DelayBar, Map
Input: None
Output: void
Pre-condition: The Game has been initialized and at least one round of play has begun.
Post-condition: The delay bar has been decremented and the map's filled-tile state has been updated for this round; loss conditions can subsequently be queried via hasLost().

Game::skipPipe
Summary: Skips the current pipe by consuming it from the head of the queue without placing it, and increments the step counter.
Algorithm:
  1. If pipeQueue is empty (no head pipe), do nothing and return.
  2. Consume the head pipe via pipeQueue.consume().
  3. Increment numOfSteps by 1.
Related Features: `numOfSteps` is incremented; delegates to PipeQueue.
Related Classes: PipeQueue
Input: None
Output: void
Pre-condition: The Game has been initialized and the pipe queue has at least one pipe (or the operation is a no-op).
Post-condition: The head pipe is removed from the queue and `numOfSteps` is incremented by 1.

Game::hasWon
Summary: Reports whether the player has won the current game, which is true when a connected path from SOURCE to SINK exists following the rules of `Map.checkPath()`.
Algorithm:
  1. Return map.checkPath().
Related Features: Delegates entirely to the underlying map's win check.
Related Classes: Map
Input: None
Output: boolean - true if the source is connected to the sink; false otherwise.
Pre-condition: The Game has been initialized and a map exists.
Post-condition: No state is changed by this query.

# Requirement
```text
 Overall/Domain description.
 Console pipe-connection game: grid with outer walls, one source inside pointing inward, one sink on the border
  pointing outward. Player places pipes from a queue; after a delay, water flows along placed pipes.
Cell[][] uses 0-based array indices, but index 0 and rows-1/cols-1 are occupied by the outer wall border. Therefore, the playable area starts at internal index 1: [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2]. Player-facing coordinates are deliberately aligned with these playable indices: row 1 maps to internal row 1, column 'A' maps to internal col 1. No row-1/col-1 conversion is performed.
 Direction provides four directions plus opposite/offset; PipeShape defines
  connection
  directions; TerminationType distinguishes SOURCE vs SINK.

  Functional Requirements

Coordinate and Direction: Coordinate.row and Coordinate.col represent internal Cell[][] array indices and are used directly as cells[row][col]. A Cell stored at cells[r][c] should have Coordinate(row=r, col=c). 
Because the outer wall border occupies index 0, playable cells naturally start at index 1, so player input aligns with internal playable indices.
  Direction enum provides four directions (UP, DOWN, LEFT, RIGHT) and Pa19Helper provides getOpposite() returning the opposite direction
  and getOffset() returning the unit coordinate offset for movement calculations.

  Game: Operations to place a pipe, skip, undo, advance water flow, check win, check loss; convenience fromString
  constructor; maintain step count. 
Operation placePipe: This method maps the player column letter to an internal column index using col - 'A' + 1, 
keeps row unchanged, and places the pipe at cells[row][colIndex]. For example, placePipe(1, 'A') targets cells[1][1].
Operation skipPipe: Consumes the current pipe from the queue and increments the step count. Operation
  undoStep: Pops the last placed cell from CellStack, restores the pipe to the queue head, clears the cell on the map,
  and increments the step count. Returns false if there are no steps to undo.

  Map: Cells are stored as a 2D array Cell[][] with indices [0..rows-1] × [0..cols-1],
  where index 0 and rows-1/cols-1 are walls (border). The playable area occupies
  internal indices [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2], which aligns with 1-based
  user input mapping. tryPlacePipe(row, col, pipe) accepts playable-area aligned coordinates (row and col in [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2]) and uses them
  directly as array indices (no conversion needed due to the wall alignment).
  It rejects: (1) row/col outside [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2], (2) non-FillableCell,
  or (3) already-occupied cell.

  Cell family: Cell.fromChar parses map chars to concrete cells; FillableCell holds an optional pipe and renders pipe or
  '.'; TerminationCell holds pointingTo direction and Type (SOURCE/SINK), with filled state for rendering; Wall renders
  wall char.

  TerminationCell.toSingleChar: Returns the corresponding arrow character based on the current termination cell's
  filling state and pointingTo direction: when filled, returns the arrow from PipePatterns.Filled; when unfilled,
  returns the arrow from PipePatterns.Unfilled. Both SOURCE and SINK use pointingTo directly without direction reversal.
  Throws IllegalStateException("Invalid pointingTo value!") for unknown direction.

  Pipe: Expose connection directions via getConnections() returning Direction[] based on Shape; char rendering by
  filled/unfilled state; construct from short string code (HZ, VT, TL, TR, BL, BR, CR). getConnections(): Returns the
  list of connection directions based on the current pipe shape; throws IllegalStateException("Unknown shape") if the
  shape is not recognized. toSingleChar(): Returns the character representation of this pipe, different for filled and
  unfilled pipes.

  Water Flow: fillBeginTile() marks the source cell as filled. fillTiles(distance) fills pipes within the specified
  distance from source using BFS-style expansion. Water propagates along pipes only when adjacent pipes have matching
  connection directions (one pipe's direction must be the opposite of the other). Each round increments the fill
  distance by 1.

  Win/Loss Conditions: checkPath() uses BFS to determine if a connected path exists from SOURCE to SINK by following
  (i) from SOURCE, step once in the SOURCE pointingTo direction, and (ii) from a pipe cell, step in each pipe connection direction.
  It does not require the traversed pipes to be filled; reaching the SINK cell implies win. hasLost() returns true when prevFilledTiles == 0,
  meaning no new pipes were filled in the previous round (loss condition). The game checks loss only after delay has ended (distance > 0).

  PipeQueue: peek/consume/undo head pipe and auto-refill to fixed length with random shapes. undo(Pipe) inserts the pipe
  back to the front of the queue.

  DelayBar: countdown() decrements the current value by 1 each round. distance() returns -currentValue, representing how
  far the water should flow (negative during countdown, positive after delay ends).

  CellStack: push/pop last placement; undoCount counts the number of successful undo actions (i.e., successful pop
  operations), not the current stack size; 

  External/Tool Classes (not generated; handwritten or reused,You only need to assume that these Java files mentioned below are already in the pa19 package.)
  Pa19Helper is a small helper/assembly class used to build core game model objects for this project. It provides
  convenience methods to (1) construct a Game by wiring together Map, PipeQueue, DelayBar, and CellStack from given
  inputs, and (2) create/parse basic elements (e.g., Map from a Cell[][] or string representation, map characters/short
  codes into Cell/Pipe). It also centralizes simple direction utilities (opposite direction and unit offsets) used
  during parsing and movement-related calculations.
  Deserializer: Purpose: deserialize map input into runtime objects. Field: Path path (input file path). Constructors:
  Deserializer(String path) delegates to private Deserializer(Path); private Deserializer(Path) validates file existence
  and throws FileNotFoundException if missing. Methods: Game parseGame() reads rows, cols, delay, map lines, and
  optional default pipes, then returns Pa19Helper.createGame(...); on unexpected EOF or I/O failure, returns null
  (and logs error). static Cell[][] parseString(int rows, int cols, String cellsRep) converts multiline text to a Cell
  matrix by character, using Pa19Helper.cellFromChar with SINK type on border cells and SOURCE type on inner
  cells. private String getFirstNonEmptyLine(BufferedReader br) returns the first non-blank, non-comment line (ignores
  lines starting with #), or null at end of stream.

  PipePatterns: Purpose: central constant repository for all map-rendering characters. Design: final utility class with
  private constructor (non-instantiable). Exposed constants: WALL (solid wall block), plus two nested static groups:
  Filled and Unfilled. Each group defines arrow chars (UP_ARROW, DOWN_ARROW, LEFT_ARROW, RIGHT_ARROW) and pipe-shape
  chars (HORIZONTAL, VERTICAL, TOP_LEFT, TOP_RIGHT, BOTTOM_LEFT, BOTTOM_RIGHT, CROSS). Use PipePatterns constants for
  all rendering chars; do not hardcode glyphs in TerminationCell and PipeShape logic.

  StringUtils: Purpose: provide lightweight string helper utilities. Class design: utility class with a private
  constructor to prevent instantiation. 
```

# Operation Specifications
Game::undoStep
Summary: Undoes the most recent successful pipe placement: removes the pipe from the map, restores it to the head of the pipe queue, and increments the step counter. Returns false if there is nothing to undo.
Algorithm:
  1. Pop the last placed FillableCell from cellStack via cellStack.pop().
  2. If the popped cell is null (nothing to undo), return false.
  3. Identify the cell's Coordinate (row, col).
  4. Read the pipe currently held by the popped cell.
  5. Restore the pipe to the front of the queue via pipeQueue.undo(pipe).
  6. Clear the cell on the map via map.undo(coord).
  7. Increment numOfSteps by 1.
  8. Return true.
Related Features: `numOfSteps` incremented; coordinates from the popped cell; cell stack's pop increments its undo counter.
Related Classes: CellStack, PipeQueue, Map, FillableCell, Coordinate, Pipe
Input: None
Output: boolean - true if an undo was performed; false if the cell stack was empty (no steps to undo).
Pre-condition: The Game has been initialized. If no successful placements have been made, this operation must return false.
Post-condition: The most recent placed pipe is removed from the map, returned to the queue's head, and `numOfSteps` is incremented by 1. The CellStack's undo count is also incremented.

Game::placePipe
Summary: Places the head pipe from the queue at the cell identified by the given player-facing row and column letter, advancing the game state (consuming the pipe, recording the placement, and incrementing the step counter) if the placement is valid.
Algorithm:
  1. Convert column letter to internal column index: colIndex = col - 'A' + 1.
  2. Keep `row` unchanged (player row 1 corresponds to internal row 1; playable area starts at index 1).
  3. If row or colIndex is outside the playable area [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2], return false (no state change).
  4. Read the head pipe via pipeQueue.peek(); if null, return false.
  5. Attempt to place the pipe via map.tryPlacePipe(row, colIndex, headPipe).
  6. If placement is successful:
     a. Push the cell (with the placed pipe) onto cellStack via cellStack.push(...).
     b. Consume the head pipe via pipeQueue.consume().
     c. Increment numOfSteps by 1.
     d. Return true.
  7. Otherwise, return false.
Related Features: `numOfSteps` (int) tracks total steps taken; delegates to pipe queue and map for placement; cell stack for undo support.
Related Classes: Map, PipeQueue, CellStack, FillableCell, Pipe, Coordinate
Input:
  - int row: 1-based player row index, which equals the internal array row index (range: [1..rows-2]).
  - char col: uppercase column letter starting at 'A' for internal col 1 (range: 'A'..column corresponding to cols-2).
Output: boolean - true if the pipe was successfully placed; false if the location is invalid or occupied.
Pre-condition: The Game has been initialized with a valid map, pipe queue, and cell stack; `col` is an uppercase letter; `row` is in [1..rows-2].
Post-condition: On true, the head pipe is removed from the queue, the cell is now occupied and pushed onto the undo stack, and `numOfSteps` is incremented by 1. On false, no state changes occur.

Game::hasLost
Summary: Reports whether the player has lost the current game, which is true when the water flow made no progress in the previous round (i.e., no new pipes were filled) and the delay has already ended.
Algorithm:
  1. If delayBar.distance() <= 0 (delay has not yet ended), return false.
  2. Return map.hasLost().
Related Features: Delegates to the map's loss state; consults the delay bar to ensure the delay has ended.
Related Classes: Map, DelayBar
Input: None
Output: boolean - true if no tiles were filled in the last water propagation round and the delay has ended; false otherwise.
Pre-condition: The Game has been initialized and a map exists.
Post-condition: No state is changed by this query.

Game::updateState
Summary: Advances the game state for one round: ticks the delay bar, then triggers the map to begin filling from the source and propagate water by the appropriate distance.
Algorithm:
  1. Decrement the delay bar by calling delayBar.countdown().
  2. Read the propagation distance via delayBar.distance().
  3. If distance >= 0 (delay has ended), call map.fillBeginTile() to mark the source as filled.
  4. Call map.fillTiles(distance) to advance water flow by the appropriate distance.
Related Features: Delegates to delayBar and map; the map tracks `prevFilledTiles`/`prevFilledDistance` for loss detection.
Related Classes: DelayBar, Map
Input: None
Output: void
Pre-condition: The Game has been initialized and at least one round of play has begun.
Post-condition: The delay bar has been decremented and the map's filled-tile state has been updated for this round; loss conditions can subsequently be queried via hasLost().

Game::skipPipe
Summary: Skips the current pipe by consuming it from the head of the queue without placing it, and increments the step counter.
Algorithm:
  1. If pipeQueue is empty (no head pipe), do nothing and return.
  2. Consume the head pipe via pipeQueue.consume().
  3. Increment numOfSteps by 1.
Related Features: `numOfSteps` is incremented; delegates to PipeQueue.
Related Classes: PipeQueue
Input: None
Output: void
Pre-condition: The Game has been initialized and the pipe queue has at least one pipe (or the operation is a no-op).
Post-condition: The head pipe is removed from the queue and `numOfSteps` is incremented by 1.

Game::hasWon
Summary: Reports whether the player has won the current game, which is true when a connected path from SOURCE to SINK exists following the rules of `Map.checkPath()`.
Algorithm:
  1. Return map.checkPath().
Related Features: Delegates entirely to the underlying map's win check.
Related Classes: Map
Input: None
Output: boolean - true if the source is connected to the sink; false otherwise.
Pre-condition: The Game has been initialized and a map exists.
Post-condition: No state is changed by this query.

  convenience methods to (1) construct a Game by wiring together Map, PipeQueue, DelayBar, and CellStack from given
  inputs, and (2) create/parse basic elements (e.g., Map from a Cell[][] or string representation, map characters/short
  codes into Cell/Pipe). It also centralizes simple direction utilities (opposite direction and unit offsets) used
  during parsing and movement-related calculations.
  Deserializer: Purpose: deserialize map input into runtime objects. Field: Path path (input file path). Constructors:
  Deserializer(String path) delegates to private Deserializer(Path); private Deserializer(Path) validates file existence
  and throws FileNotFoundException if missing. Methods: Game parseGame() reads rows, cols, delay, map lines, and
  optional default pipes, then returns Pa19Helper.createGame(...); on unexpected EOF or I/O failure, returns null
  (and logs error). static Cell[][] parseString(int rows, int cols, String cellsRep) converts multiline text to a Cell
  matrix by character, using Pa19Helper.cellFromChar with SINK type on border cells and SOURCE type on inner
  cells. private String getFirstNonEmptyLine(BufferedReader br) returns the first non-blank, non-comment line (ignores
  lines starting with #), or null at end of stream.

  PipePatterns: Purpose: central constant repository for all map-rendering characters. Design: final utility class with
  private constructor (non-instantiable). Exposed constants: WALL (solid wall block), plus two nested static groups:
  Filled and Unfilled. Each group defines arrow chars (UP_ARROW, DOWN_ARROW, LEFT_ARROW, RIGHT_ARROW) and pipe-shape
  chars (HORIZONTAL, VERTICAL, TOP_LEFT, TOP_RIGHT, BOTTOM_LEFT, BOTTOM_RIGHT, CROSS). Use PipePatterns constants for
  all rendering chars; do not hardcode glyphs in TerminationCell and PipeShape logic.

  StringUtils: Purpose: provide lightweight string helper utilities. Class design: utility class with a private
  constructor to prevent instantiation.

# Operation Specifications
Game::undoStep
Summary: Undoes the most recent successful pipe placement: removes the pipe from the map, restores it to the head of the pipe queue, and increments the step counter. Returns false if there is nothing to undo.
Algorithm:
  1. Pop the last placed FillableCell from cellStack via cellStack.pop().
  2. If the popped cell is null (nothing to undo), return false.
  3. Identify the cell's Coordinate (row, col).
  4. Read the pipe currently held by the popped cell.
  5. Restore the pipe to the front of the queue via pipeQueue.undo(pipe).
  6. Clear the cell on the map via map.undo(coord).
  7. Increment numOfSteps by 1.
  8. Return true.
Related Features: `numOfSteps` incremented; coordinates from the popped cell; cell stack's pop increments its undo counter.
Related Classes: CellStack, PipeQueue, Map, FillableCell, Coordinate, Pipe
Input: None
Output: boolean - true if an undo was performed; false if the cell stack was empty (no steps to undo).
Pre-condition: The Game has been initialized. If no successful placements have been made, this operation must return false.
Post-condition: The most recent placed pipe is removed from the map, returned to the queue's head, and `numOfSteps` is incremented by 1. The CellStack's undo count is also incremented.

Game::placePipe
Summary: Places the head pipe from the queue at the cell identified by the given player-facing row and column letter, advancing the game state (consuming the pipe, recording the placement, and incrementing the step counter) if the placement is valid.
Algorithm:
  1. Convert column letter to internal column index: colIndex = col - 'A' + 1.
  2. Keep `row` unchanged (player row 1 corresponds to internal row 1; playable area starts at index 1).
  3. If row or colIndex is outside the playable area [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2], return false (no state change).
  4. Read the head pipe via pipeQueue.peek(); if null, return false.
  5. Attempt to place the pipe via map.tryPlacePipe(row, colIndex, headPipe).
  6. If placement is successful:
     a. Push the cell (with the placed pipe) onto cellStack via cellStack.push(...).
     b. Consume the head pipe via pipeQueue.consume().
     c. Increment numOfSteps by 1.
     d. Return true.
  7. Otherwise, return false.
Related Features: `numOfSteps` (int) tracks total steps taken; delegates to pipe queue and map for placement; cell stack for undo support.
Related Classes: Map, PipeQueue, CellStack, FillableCell, Pipe, Coordinate
Input:
  - int row: 1-based player row index, which equals the internal array row index (range: [1..rows-2]).
  - char col: uppercase column letter starting at 'A' for internal col 1 (range: 'A'..column corresponding to cols-2).
Output: boolean - true if the pipe was successfully placed; false if the location is invalid or occupied.
Pre-condition: The Game has been initialized with a valid map, pipe queue, and cell stack; `col` is an uppercase letter; `row` is in [1..rows-2].
Post-condition: On true, the head pipe is removed from the queue, the cell is now occupied and pushed onto the undo stack, and `numOfSteps` is incremented by 1. On false, no state changes occur.

Game::hasLost
Summary: Reports whether the player has lost the current game, which is true when the water flow made no progress in the previous round (i.e., no new pipes were filled) and the delay has already ended.
Algorithm:
  1. If delayBar.distance() <= 0 (delay has not yet ended), return false.
  2. Return map.hasLost().
Related Features: Delegates to the map's loss state; consults the delay bar to ensure the delay has ended.
Related Classes: Map, DelayBar
Input: None
Output: boolean - true if no tiles were filled in the last water propagation round and the delay has ended; false otherwise.
Pre-condition: The Game has been initialized and a map exists.
Post-condition: No state is changed by this query.

Game::updateState
Summary: Advances the game state for one round: ticks the delay bar, then triggers the map to begin filling from the source and propagate water by the appropriate distance.
Algorithm:
  1. Decrement the delay bar by calling delayBar.countdown().
  2. Read the propagation distance via delayBar.distance().
  3. If distance >= 0 (delay has ended), call map.fillBeginTile() to mark the source as filled.
  4. Call map.fillTiles(distance) to advance water flow by the appropriate distance.
Related Features: Delegates to delayBar and map; the map tracks `prevFilledTiles`/`prevFilledDistance` for loss detection.
Related Classes: DelayBar, Map
Input: None
Output: void
Pre-condition: The Game has been initialized and at least one round of play has begun.
Post-condition: The delay bar has been decremented and the map's filled-tile state has been updated for this round; loss conditions can subsequently be queried via hasLost().

Game::skipPipe
Summary: Skips the current pipe by consuming it from the head of the queue without placing it, and increments the step counter.
Algorithm:
  1. If pipeQueue is empty (no head pipe), do nothing and return.
  2. Consume the head pipe via pipeQueue.consume().
  3. Increment numOfSteps by 1.
Related Features: `numOfSteps` is incremented; delegates to PipeQueue.
Related Classes: PipeQueue
Input: None
Output: void
Pre-condition: The Game has been initialized and the pipe queue has at least one pipe (or the operation is a no-op).
Post-condition: The head pipe is removed from the queue and `numOfSteps` is incremented by 1.

Game::hasWon
Summary: Reports whether the player has won the current game, which is true when a connected path from SOURCE to SINK exists following the rules of `Map.checkPath()`.
Algorithm:
  1. Return map.checkPath().
Related Features: Delegates entirely to the underlying map's win check.
Related Classes: Map
Input: None
Output: boolean - true if the source is connected to the sink; false otherwise.
Pre-condition: The Game has been initialized and a map exists.
Post-condition: No state is changed by this query.

# Task
You will be given a **Requirement** and a **Class Diagram** in PlantUML. Your task is to annotate every operation listed in **Operations** with a specification.

An operation specification must describe the following sections about the operation:
1. Summary: the summary of functionality;
2. Algorithm: algorithm or pseudo code;
3. Related Features: a list of structural or behavior features within this class that shall be accessed;
4. Related Classes: a list of classes and data types defined in **Class Diagram** that shall be accessed, in the format of `Related Classes: ClsA, CLsB, ...` or `Related Classes: None`;
5. Input: the input parameters, including the meaning, the format, and the value ranges if necessary;
6. Output: output value, including the meaning, the format, and the value ranges if necessary;
7. Pre-condition: the condition that the system and the input must satisfy before the operation is executed;
8. Post-condition: the condition that the system and the output must satisfy after the operation is executed.

Finish this task by following the guidelines below.
1. Take the principle of modularization into account.
2. For each operation, determine its functional boundary based on the given requirement. Ensure high cohesion and low coupling.
3. If there is any unspecified details, such as undefined constants, rates, and ratios, then you must infer them.
4. Make sure that all requirements can be covered.

# Requirement
```text
 Overall/Domain description.
 Console pipe-connection game: grid with outer walls, one source inside pointing inward, one sink on the border
  pointing outward. Player places pipes from a queue; after a delay, water flows along placed pipes.
Cell[][] uses 0-based array indices, but index 0 and rows-1/cols-1 are occupied by the outer wall border. Therefore, the playable area starts at internal index 1: [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2]. Player-facing coordinates are deliberately aligned with these playable indices: row 1 maps to internal row 1, column 'A' maps to internal col 1. No row-1/col-1 conversion is performed.
 Direction provides four directions plus opposite/offset; PipeShape defines
  connection
  directions; TerminationType distinguishes SOURCE vs SINK.

  Functional Requirements

Coordinate and Direction: Coordinate.row and Coordinate.col represent internal Cell[][] array indices and are used directly as cells[row][col]. A Cell stored at cells[r][c] should have Coordinate(row=r, col=c). 
Because the outer wall border occupies index 0, playable cells naturally start at index 1, so player input aligns with internal playable indices.
  Direction enum provides four directions (UP, DOWN, LEFT, RIGHT) and Pa19Helper provides getOpposite() returning the opposite direction
  and getOffset() returning the unit coordinate offset for movement calculations.

  Game: Operations to place a pipe, skip, undo, advance water flow, check win, check loss; convenience fromString
  constructor; maintain step count. 
Operation placePipe: This method maps the player column letter to an internal column index using col - 'A' + 1, 
keeps row unchanged, and places the pipe at cells[row][colIndex]. For example, placePipe(1, 'A') targets cells[1][1].
Operation skipPipe: Consumes the current pipe from the queue and increments the step count. Operation
  undoStep: Pops the last placed cell from CellStack, restores the pipe to the queue head, clears the cell on the map,
  and increments the step count. Returns false if there are no steps to undo.

  Map: Cells are stored as a 2D array Cell[][] with indices [0..rows-1] × [0..cols-1],
  where index 0 and rows-1/cols-1 are walls (border). The playable area occupies
  internal indices [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2], which aligns with 1-based
  user input mapping. tryPlacePipe(row, col, pipe) accepts playable-area aligned coordinates (row and col in [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2]) and uses them
  directly as array indices (no conversion needed due to the wall alignment).
  It rejects: (1) row/col outside [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2], (2) non-FillableCell,
  or (3) already-occupied cell.

  Cell family: Cell.fromChar parses map chars to concrete cells; FillableCell holds an optional pipe and renders pipe or
  '.'; TerminationCell holds pointingTo direction and Type (SOURCE/SINK), with filled state for rendering; Wall renders
  wall char.

  TerminationCell.toSingleChar: Returns the corresponding arrow character based on the current termination cell's
  filling state and pointingTo direction: when filled, returns the arrow from PipePatterns.Filled; when unfilled,
  returns the arrow from PipePatterns.Unfilled. Both SOURCE and SINK use pointingTo directly without direction reversal.
  Throws IllegalStateException("Invalid pointingTo value!") for unknown direction.

  Pipe: Expose connection directions via getConnections() returning Direction[] based on Shape; char rendering by
  filled/unfilled state; construct from short string code (HZ, VT, TL, TR, BL, BR, CR). getConnections(): Returns the
  list of connection directions based on the current pipe shape; throws IllegalStateException("Unknown shape") if the
  shape is not recognized. toSingleChar(): Returns the character representation of this pipe, different for filled and
  unfilled pipes.

  Water Flow: fillBeginTile() marks the source cell as filled. fillTiles(distance) fills pipes within the specified
  distance from source using BFS-style expansion. Water propagates along pipes only when adjacent pipes have matching
  connection directions (one pipe's direction must be the opposite of the other). Each round increments the fill
  distance by 1.

  Win/Loss Conditions: checkPath() uses BFS to determine if a connected path exists from SOURCE to SINK by following
  (i) from SOURCE, step once in the SOURCE pointingTo direction, and (ii) from a pipe cell, step in each pipe connection direction.
  It does not require the traversed pipes to be filled; reaching the SINK cell implies win. hasLost() returns true when prevFilledTiles == 0,
  meaning no new pipes were filled in the previous round (loss condition). The game checks loss only after delay has ended (distance > 0).

  PipeQueue: peek/consume/undo head pipe and auto-refill to fixed length with random shapes. undo(Pipe) inserts the pipe
  back to the front of the queue.

  DelayBar: countdown() decrements the current value by 1 each round. distance() returns -currentValue, representing how
  far the water should flow (negative during countdown, positive after delay ends).

  CellStack: push/pop last placement; undoCount counts the number of successful undo actions (i.e., successful pop
  operations), not the current stack size; 

  External/Tool Classes (not generated; handwritten or reused,You only need to assume that these Java files mentioned below are already in the pa19 package.)
  Pa19Helper is a small helper/assembly class used to build core game model objects for this project. It provides
  convenience methods to (1) construct a Game by wiring together Map, PipeQueue, DelayBar, and CellStack from given
  inputs, and (2) create/parse basic elements (e.g., Map from a Cell[][] or string representation, map characters/short
  codes into Cell/Pipe). It also centralizes simple direction utilities (opposite direction and unit offsets) used
  during parsing and movement-related calculations.
  Deserializer: Purpose: deserialize map input into runtime objects. Field: Path path (input file path). Constructors:
  Deserializer(String path) delegates to private Deserializer(Path); private Deserializer(Path) validates file existence
  and throws FileNotFoundException if missing. Methods: Game parseGame() reads rows, cols, delay, map lines, and
  optional default pipes, then returns Pa19Helper.createGame(...); on unexpected EOF or I/O failure, returns null
  (and logs error). static Cell[][] parseString(int rows, int cols, String cellsRep) converts multiline text to a Cell
  matrix by character, using Pa19Helper.cellFromChar with SINK type on border cells and SOURCE type on inner
  cells. private String getFirstNonEmptyLine(BufferedReader br) returns the first non-blank, non-comment line (ignores
  lines starting with #), or null at end of stream.

  PipePatterns: Purpose: central constant repository for all map-rendering characters. Design: final utility class with
  private constructor (non-instantiable). Exposed constants: WALL (solid wall block), plus two nested static groups:
  Filled and Unfilled. Each group defines arrow chars (UP_ARROW, DOWN_ARROW, LEFT_ARROW, RIGHT_ARROW) and pipe-shape
  chars (HORIZONTAL, VERTICAL, TOP_LEFT, TOP_RIGHT, BOTTOM_LEFT, BOTTOM_RIGHT, CROSS). Use PipePatterns constants for
  all rendering chars; do not hardcode glyphs in TerminationCell and PipeShape logic.

  StringUtils: Purpose: provide lightweight string helper utilities. Class design: utility class with a private
  constructor to prevent instantiation.

# Requirement
```text
 Overall/Domain description.
 Console pipe-connection game: grid with outer walls, one source inside pointing inward, one sink on the border
  pointing outward. Player places pipes from a queue; after a delay, water flows along placed pipes.
Cell[][] uses 0-based array indices, but index 0 and rows-1/cols-1 are occupied by the outer wall border. Therefore, the playable area starts at internal index 1: [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2]. Player-facing coordinates are deliberately aligned with these playable indices: row 1 maps to internal row 1, column 'A' maps to internal col 1. No row-1/col-1 conversion is performed.
 Direction provides four directions plus opposite/offset; PipeShape defines
  connection
  directions; TerminationType distinguishes SOURCE vs SINK.

  Functional Requirements

Coordinate and Direction: Coordinate.row and Coordinate.col represent internal Cell[][] array indices and are used directly as cells[row][col]. A Cell stored at cells[r][c] should have Coordinate(row=r, col=c). 
Because the outer wall border occupies index 0, playable cells naturally start at index 1, so player input aligns with internal playable indices.
  Direction enum provides four directions (UP, DOWN, LEFT, RIGHT) and Pa19Helper provides getOpposite() returning the opposite direction
  and getOffset() returning the unit coordinate offset for movement calculations.

  Game: Operations to place a pipe, skip, undo, advance water flow, check win, check loss; convenience fromString
  constructor; maintain step count. 
Operation placePipe: This method maps the player column letter to an internal column index using col - 'A' + 1, 
keeps row unchanged, and places the pipe at cells[row][colIndex]. For example, placePipe(1, 'A') targets cells[1][1].
Operation skipPipe: Consumes the current pipe from the queue and increments the step count. Operation
  undoStep: Pops the last placed cell from CellStack, restores the pipe to the queue head, clears the cell on the map,
  and increments the step count. Returns false if there are no steps to undo.

  Map: Cells are stored as a 2D array Cell[][] with indices [0..rows-1] × [0..cols-1],
  where index 0 and rows-1/cols-1 are walls (border). The playable area occupies
  internal indices [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2], which aligns with 1-based
  user input mapping. tryPlacePipe(row, col, pipe) accepts playable-area aligned coordinates (row and col in [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2]) and uses them
  directly as array indices (no conversion needed due to the wall alignment).
  It rejects: (1) row/col outside [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2], (2) non-FillableCell,
  or (3) already-occupied cell.

  Cell family: Cell.fromChar parses map chars to concrete cells; FillableCell holds an optional pipe and renders pipe or
  '.'; TerminationCell holds pointingTo direction and Type (SOURCE/SINK), with filled state for rendering; Wall renders
  wall char.

  TerminationCell.toSingleChar: Returns the corresponding arrow character based on the current termination cell's
  filling state and pointingTo direction: when filled, returns the arrow from PipePatterns.Filled; when unfilled,
  returns the arrow from PipePatterns.Unfilled. Both SOURCE and SINK use pointingTo directly without direction reversal.
  Throws IllegalStateException("Invalid pointingTo value!") for unknown direction.

  Pipe: Expose connection directions via getConnections() returning Direction[] based on Shape; char rendering by
  filled/unfilled state; construct from short string code (HZ, VT, TL, TR, BL, BR, CR). getConnections(): Returns the
  list of connection directions based on the current pipe shape; throws IllegalStateException("Unknown shape") if the
  shape is not recognized. toSingleChar(): Returns the character representation of this pipe, different for filled and
  unfilled pipes.

  Water Flow: fillBeginTile() marks the source cell as filled. fillTiles(distance) fills pipes within the specified
  distance from source using BFS-style expansion. Water propagates along pipes only when adjacent pipes have matching
  connection directions (one pipe's direction must be the opposite of the other). Each round increments the fill
  distance by 1.

  Win/Loss Conditions: checkPath() uses BFS to determine if a connected path exists from SOURCE to SINK by following
  (i) from SOURCE, step once in the SOURCE pointingTo direction, and (ii) from a pipe cell, step in each pipe connection direction.
  It does not require the traversed pipes to be filled; reaching the SINK cell implies win. hasLost() returns true when prevFilledTiles == 0,
  meaning no new pipes were filled in the previous round (loss condition). The game checks loss only after delay has ended (distance > 0).

  PipeQueue: peek/consume/undo head pipe and auto-refill to fixed length with random shapes. undo(Pipe) inserts the pipe
  back to the front of the queue.

  DelayBar: countdown() decrements the current value by 1 each round. distance() returns -currentValue, representing how
  far the water should flow (negative during countdown, positive after delay ends).

  CellStack: push/pop last placement; undoCount counts the number of successful undo actions (i.e., successful pop
  operations), not the current stack size; 

  External/Tool Classes (not generated; handwritten or reused,You only need to assume that these Java files mentioned below are already in the pa19 package.)
  Pa19Helper is a small helper/assembly class used to build core game model objects for this project. It provides
  convenience methods to (1) construct a Game by wiring together Map, PipeQueue, DelayBar, and CellStack from given
  inputs, and (2) create/parse basic elements (e.g., Map from a Cell[][] or string representation, map characters/short
  codes into Cell/Pipe). It also centralizes simple direction utilities (opposite direction and unit offsets) used
  during parsing and movement-related calculations.
  Deserializer: Purpose: deserialize map input into runtime objects. Field: Path path (input file path). Constructors:
  Deserializer(String path) delegates to private Deserializer(Path); private Deserializer(Path) validates file existence
  and throws FileNotFoundException if missing. Methods: Game parseGame() reads rows, cols, delay, map lines, and
  optional default pipes, then returns Pa19Helper.createGame(...); on unexpected EOF or I/O failure, returns null
  (and logs error). static Cell[][] parseString(int rows, int cols, String cellsRep) converts multiline text to a Cell
  matrix by character, using Pa19Helper.cellFromChar with SINK type on border cells and SOURCE type on inner
  cells. private String getFirstNonEmptyLine(BufferedReader br) returns the first non-blank, non-comment line (ignores
  lines starting with #), or null at end of stream.

  PipePatterns: Purpose: central constant repository for all map-rendering characters. Design: final utility class with
  private constructor (non-instantiable). Exposed constants: WALL (solid wall block), plus two nested static groups:
  Filled and Unfilled. Each group defines arrow chars (UP_ARROW, DOWN_ARROW, LEFT_ARROW, RIGHT_ARROW) and pipe-shape
  chars (HORIZONTAL, VERTICAL, TOP_LEFT, TOP_RIGHT, BOTTOM_LEFT, BOTTOM_RIGHT, CROSS). Use PipePatterns constants for
  all rendering chars; do not hardcode glyphs in TerminationCell and PipeShape logic.

  StringUtils: Purpose: provide lightweight string helper utilities. Class design: utility class with a private
  constructor to prevent instantiation. 
```
